Please confirm, against the code, what the text now says each result is:
  > 
  > 1. **Variance** (Results, "Variance"; abstract; Appendix Fig A2B): the slopes -0.50 (n), +0.55 [0.547, 0.556] (1+d), -0.50 (p(1-p)) are on **log SD** of the Chin regression over **42 cells of the plain SBM, Bernoulli, sigma = 0.5: the null column and mechanism (a) at s = 1/2** (`c1_exponents`); the L exponents (n^-0.02, (1+d)^1.09, [p(1-p)]^-0.99) are over 210 graph draws.
  > 2. **Absolute R2 of log |bias|** (Results, "gains must be read next to"): on the 1224 cells with an exact prediction, S-bar -0.22, S_adj -0.06, corner x curvature -0.12, p(1-p) -0.26 (`bias_reference.csv`), exact prediction 0.987. I no longer say "above a constant": there is no constant row for log |bias| in the tables, so the text says "negative absolute held-out R2". Is that right? The appendix says "2178 cells" for the log RMSE R2s.
  > 3. **Definitions in Design** (new): a *cell* = one combination of graph, degree, assignment design, p, mechanism, spillover share, noise level; *ties* = cells outside D; D* = the part of D in which misfit of the specification supplies at least 20% of the variance of the estimate (`sel_share` >= 0.2, chosen on the other half of the draws). Please correct any of these.
  > 4. **Appendix**: Dependence on p (seven panels; RMSE minimiser 0.40 for (c) and 0.60 for (g) at d = 20); Grid (R6 for Stanford3 / ego-Facebook as you wrote; the extension list); a new paragraph "Fitted-form oracle" with Fig A9 (the numbers from `or_fit_check.csv`: shares at a grid end 5/59/86% for (c), 59/82/86% for (e); RMSE fitted vs known 0.087/0.087, 0.549/0.233, 2.00/0.541 for (c); spread 0.05% at d = 20 for (c)); Discussion: (e) bias prediction outside the interval in 10% of its cells.
  > 5. **Coverage by family** (Results, "Confidence intervals"): Stanford3 0.52, ego-Facebook 0.66, Watts-Strogatz 0.82 on the 1800 `figure` cells: please confirm against `c8_coverage_by_family.csv`.
  > 
  > One question for your decision. The review of version 1 (M6) says that cluster Horvitz-Thompson and a graph-neural-network estimator, which the paper lists as not run, must be run or shown infeasible before the final version. The starter literature lists both families. A cluster HT estimator on the cluster-design cells and a small GNN (own treatment plus neighbours' treatments as input, prediction at the two corners, graph-cluster cross-validation) on the Tier A sample of cells look feasible on CPU at n = 3000. If you can run them, deliver the cells with their intervals; if you judge them infeasible within the budget, say why in one line and the paper will say so. I will place whatever is delivered.

I recorded my reading of the floor result in Brief rev. 13, before any block result is read: B₂ κ̂ = 0.25 is a bound, not a located minimum; P6(1) on the block then tests only out-of-sample coverage ≥ 0.90 and is not evidence of calibration (the paper calls B₂ conservative unless the oracle/HC0 width ratios say otherwise); the (d) rule stays as written (bound 4); no grid move, and any extension below 0.25 is exploratory. The discriminating results are C2/C3, the tails and the oracle width ratio. Please report the width ratio to the oracle and to HC0 on near-zero-bias cells with the block results. Nothing else needed from you until the block ends.
